Question: A sample consisting of five observations has an arithmetic mean of \(10\) and a median of \(12.\) The smallest value that the range (largest observation minus smallest) can assume for such a sample is
Solution:
The median controls the middle observation after sorting, while the mean controls the total. The five observations sum to
\[
5\cdot10=50.
\]
Since the median is \(12\), the middle observation and the two larger observations are each at least \(12\). Their sum is therefore at least \(36\), leaving a sum of at most
\[
50-36=14
\]
for the lower two observations.

At least one of those lower observations must be at most \(7\); if both were greater than \(7\), their sum would exceed \(14\). The largest observation is at least \(12\), so every such sample has range at least
\[
12-7=5.
\]
This bound is attained by
\[
7,\ 7,\ 12,\ 12,\ 12.
\]
Its sum is \(50\), its median is \(12\), and its range is \(12-7=5\). Thus the smallest possible range is \(\boxed{5}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
